title: Can We Bring Back Extinct Species? | De Extinction Explained
description:
From Jurassic Park to real-world labs, the idea of bringing back extinct animals — called de-extinction or resurrection biology — has fascinated scientists and the public alike. But is it really possible to resurrect creatures like the Woolly Mammoth, Dodo, or Sabre-Toothed Tiger using today’s technology?

In this episode of Pale Blue Thoughts, we explore the science and myths behind resurrection biology:

The cloning revolution and the story of Dolly the Sheep.

How scientists are using somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) and CRISPR genome editing.

Projects to revive the Woolly Mammoth, Passenger Pigeon, Quagga, and Dire Wolf.

The difference between cloning, back-breeding, and genome editing.

The massive challenges: DNA degradation, surrogate species, and ecological risks.

Why resurrecting dinosaurs is impossible — but creating a “Pleistocene Park” might happen.

The ethical question: Should we bring back the dead when so many living species are endangered?

👉 If you’ve searched for resurrection biology explained, de-extinction science, cloning Dolly sheep, Woolly Mammoth revival, CRISPR de-extinction, Jurassic Park science, passenger pigeon resurrection, Quagga project, Pleistocene Park, cloning extinct animals — this video dives into the facts vs fiction.
